newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian stocks slip, trading seen volatile.
newsitem.headline: Austrian stocks slip, trading seen volatile.

text.p: Austria's blue-chip ATX index clawed back most of earlier losses to end moderately lower on Monday and traders said the outlook for the market was promising.
Weak international markets early on in the morning drove the ATX index down as low as 1,409.65 points, but it recovered to close 0.49 percent lower at 1,425.59.
"It was a bit exaggerated at the start -- obviously some people desperately wanted to get," said one trader, who traced today's selling pressure to market makers not investors.
Support on technical charts at around 1,410 points had held up well, traders said.
"The intra-day reversal is a positive sign. Technically things look good," said another trader.
Trading is expected to remain volatile due to dwindling turnover.
"There're only buy orders coming in from the international side," said a trader, who expects the ATX to head for 1,430 then 1,450 points barring any negative news.
Of the ATX's 21 constituents, eight rose while 13 fell. Lenzing led ATX gainers, up 2.69 percent at 895 and Brau-Union headed decliners, down 2.3 percent at 806.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index fell 0.55 percent to 512.98 points.
The August ATX future lost 1.2 points to 1,427 on turnover of 3,435 contracts.
